transcript:
Meeting header: Date/Time 2025-03-10 15:00 UTC; Duration ~45m; Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lena (BrightHealth Head of MLOps), Marcus (Infra), Priya (Product), Noah (SRE)

Summary: POC weekly sync - dedicated sizing and autoscaling. Focused on capacity planning, autoscale policies, burst handling, warm pools/pre-warm, fallback to hosted API, and cost/latency tradeoffs.

Topics: Dedicated sizing, autoscaling thresholds, burst capacity, warm-pool pre-warming, fallback strategies, SLA/p95 latency targets, telemetry to measure cost.

[00:00] Ava Martinez (Redwood AE): Alright everyone thanks for joining. well do a quick recap from last week then dive into the sizing spreadsheet and the burst scenarios that Marcus sent over.
[00:18] Lena Cho (BrightHealth): thanks ava, yep we got good feedback from product on the initial perf numbers. main priority is p95 < 450ms for the clinical inference path, and cost can't exceed current budget by more than 30%.
[00:30] Marcus Nguyen (Infra): quick note — our traffic is pretty spiky, we've got scheduled ETL jobs that fan out inference bursts for batch scoring, plus interactive usage during clinic hours 9-11 and 15-17. spikes can multiply qps 3–5x for a few minutes.
[00:50] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): ok that helps. so there are two dimensions we usually tune: baseline reserved capacity to hit steady-state p95 SLO, and burst capacity for those short spikes. options are: reserved Dedicated gpus, a warm pool, or fallback to Redwood hosted API for extra headroom. each has cost/latency implications.
[01:10] Priya Sharma (Product): can you remind us the difference between warm pool vs autoscale? we've heard both terms interchanged.
[01:20] Diego Ramos (Redwood SE): sure. autoscale dynamically spins up extra nodes when queue length or cpu/gpu util crosses thresholds — that can add 30–120s depending on node boot/initialization. warm pool keeps nodes already provisioned but idle so they can accept requests in <10s. that reduces cold-start tail latency but you pay for some idle capacity.
[01:40] Noah Lee (SRE): what's the typical pre-warm size you recommend for a 3–5x spike scenario?
[01:46] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): rule of thumb: provision warm pool for 30–50% of expected peak to smooth short spikes, the rest can be handled by quick autoscale or hosted fallback. so for a 5x spike on a baseline of 20 concurrent requests, warm pool of ~40 concurrent capacity helps.
[02:05] Marcus Nguyen (Infra): our baseline average concurrent is actually closer to 18, peak to 90 for a few min during batch windows. so 40 would be a big chunk. cost looks scary.
[02:20] Ava Martinez (Redwood AE): that's where quantization and batching come in — Samir, can you summarize the value there?
[02:25] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): yeah. moving to an int8 quantized variant can cut GPU mem and throughput cost by roughly 2–3x for many models with modest quality drop; also request-level batching or continuous batching reduces per-token cost if latency SLO allows a 20–40ms extra response window. we put numbers in the sizing sheet.
[02:50] Lena Cho (BrightHealth): we ran a quick A/B with int8 on a dev model — quality looks ok for most clinic templates but a small subset regressed. question is can Redwood do automatic fallbacks to FP16 for flagged prompts?
[03:05] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): yes, we can configure model variant routing: match certain prompt types or a heuristic (entropy/confidence) to route to higher-precision model. that impacts cost but keeps correctness for critical prompts.
[03:20] Priya Sharma (Product): curious about burst billing and granularity — is billing per GPU-hour or per-minute in Dedicated?
[03:26] Ava Martinez (Redwood AE): Dedicated is reserved capacity by the pool, billed monthly for reserved; we also offer burst credit/spot pool options that are metered differently. in the spreadsheet we show equivalent per-minute marginal cost for bursts so you can compare.
[03:40] Marcus Nguyen (Infra): one operational concern: network egress and VPC peering with our cluster. in private mode we need to ensure no cross-tenant leakage and KMS integration for keys. can you share the security docs?
[03:53] Diego Ramos (Redwood SE): yes we have SOC2 + KMS guides, and the private deployment doc. i'll drop the links after the call.
[04:00] Ava Martinez (Redwood AE): great. back to sizing — Samir can you walk through the recommended config you put in the sheet?
[04:07] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): sure. sheet scenario A is conservative: baseline reserved pool = 4 x A100-80GB equiv nodes, warm pool = 2 nodes (kept hot), autoscale up-to 8 nodes on demand, burst fallback to hosted up to 6 concurrent requests. this aims to hold p95 under 450ms for median workloads. scenario B is cost-optimised: baseline 2 nodes with a larger warm pool on cheaper quantized variants + aggressive batch windows, autoscale to 6 nodes. B reduces monthly cost ~38% vs A at expense of more complexity.
[05:00] Lena Cho (BrightHealth): which scenario handled the 90 concurrent peak we saw?
[05:06] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): A can handle 90 with autoscale and fallback; B would struggle unless we increase warm pool. we did a quick calc: to handle a blunt 90 concurrent at p95 <450ms you'd need roughly baseline eq of 6–7 A100 nodes unless batching/quantize reduces per-request GPU work. we put the numbers in the "expected throughput" column.
[05:30] Marcus Nguyen (Infra): can you show the math quickly? I remember last week's sheet but want to ensure we understand assumptions.
[05:36] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): assumptions: model tokens per request ~200, decoder-only autoreg cost approx tokens * 2 FLOPS factor, int8 gives 2.5x speedup, batching avg 6 req/batch for interactive peaks. those are coarse but we calibrated with your trace.
[06:00] Priya Sharma (Product): where's the trace again? I think Marcus uploaded a truncated sample.
[06:05] Marcus Nguyen (Infra): yes I uploaded to the shared drive; will add the full 7-day trace today.
[06:12] Ava Martinez (Redwood AE): perfect. next, latency tail — cold starts from autoscale were my worry. can we pre-warm model weights in <10s?
[06:22] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): depends on model size; 70B models need ~20–40s to load in many cases, but we can use a segmented loading strategy and keep a warm pool of smaller instances that can immediately accept requests while larger nodes finish KV cache warmup. also KV cache warmness matters for long-context sessions.
[06:40] Noah Lee (SRE): what's KV cache warmup behavior for sessionized clinical dialogs? we often have multi-turn flows.
[06:46] Diego Ramos (Redwood SE): KV cache benefits repeated tokens in a session; if sessions are long we recommend sticky routing to same node or a small session-affinity layer so you avoid reloading cache; that was in the ops recommendations.
[07:05] Lena Cho (BrightHealth): on the security front, we need audit logs and token-level tracing for a SOC2 control. is that available in Dedicated?
[07:12] Diego Ramos (Redwood SE): yes audit logs, KMS key control, and RBAC are available for Dedicated and Private. we'll attach the compliance pack after the call.
[07:25] Ava Martinez (Redwood AE): ok let's move to the burst examples you sent Marcus, the 3-minute ETL spike scenario — how to handle that cheaply?
[07:34] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): cheap approach: pre-schedule a temporary warm pool increase during ETL windows — e.g., increase warm pool by 3 nodes during 02:00-02:10 local time; that avoids autoscale cold starts. if spikes are unpredictable, use hosted fallback which is instant but adds cross-service latency (~30–80ms) and egress cost.
[07:57] Marcus Nguyen (Infra): fallback latency plus egress might push us over p95. we need measurement.
[08:05] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): agreed — that's why we propose hybrid: reserved for most critical clinical route, fallback for lower-critical batch jobs. We can tag routes by priority.
[08:20] Priya Sharma (Product): question on SLA — if we use fallback to hosted, is there a guaranteed network path?
[08:26] Ava Martinez (Redwood AE): hosted path goes over TLS outbound from your VPC to Redwood's hosted endpoints with private peering options in some regions. it's not pinned to your Dedicated GPUs but it's resilient; for enterprise customers we can negotiate egress guarantees.
[08:40] Lena Cho (BrightHealth): ok that covers most. one more: observability — we'll need token-level cost and latency dashboards to reconcile billing.
[08:48] Diego Ramos (Redwood SE): Redwood Console provides per-route token-level cost, latency percentiles, and error traces; we can set alerts on p95 and unexpected cost drift.
[09:00] Ava Martinez (Redwood AE): good. action recap: Samir to model the warm-pool scenarios and prepare an autoscale policy template; Diego to share security/compliance docs; Ava to send sizing spreadsheet + cost calc. Marcus and Lena to share traces and stakeholder list. we'll schedule the benchmark next week.
[09:25] Marcus Nguyen (Infra): timeline wise we need the spreadsheet by Thursday so we can put numbers into procurement.
[09:30] Ava Martinez (Redwood AE): we'll get it to you by Wednesday EOD, aiming for 2025-03-12.
[09:36] Priya Sharma (Product): for the benchmark run, can we include a scripted mix of interactive and batch traffic?
[09:42] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): yes we'll set up a mixed workload harness — interactive QPS profile + batch bursts; we'll include warm-pool toggles and quantized vs FP routes.
[09:53] Lena Cho (BrightHealth): perfect. thanks all.

Questions raised: "Can Redwood route to FP16 for flagged prompts?" "How long to pre-warm for 70B models?" "What's the cost delta for warm pool vs autoscale?"
